description:
As I live on a classified road, I am required to apply for planning permission. I would like to apply for a vehicular crossover/dropped kerb outside my property in order to create a driveway for off-street parking. There are a number of important and pressing reasons to support this request:

Firstly, my elderly mother, who is a resident at this address, following knee surgery, continues to struggle with mobility issues. Having access to a driveway would significantly improve her access to the home, reducing the risk of trips or falls, particularly when entering or exiting a vehicle. Being able to park directly outside the home would also reduce the physical strain she currently experiences when walking from her car to the front door.

Secondly, the area directly outside the property currently contains loose pebbles, which have unfortunately become a source of anti-social behaviour. These pebbles are often picked up by local youths and thrown at the nearby bus shelter, which has resulted in the shelter being vandalised and shattered on at least six occasions over the past three months. This not only poses a danger to the public with broken glass but also requires repeated interventions by TFL, incurring costs for repairs. Replacing this pebbled area with a paved driveway would eliminate the availability of these stones, thereby removing a key factor contributing to the vandalism and enhancing public safety.

Additional supporting factors include:

Increase in vehicle thefts in the area: off road parking will help improve security and give me a greater peace of mind by having visibility of my vehicle

Reducing On-Street Parking Pressure: Creating an off-street parking space will free up on-road parking for other residents and visitors, helping to ease congestion in a high-demand residential area.

Improved Aesthetics and Property Value: The installation of a professionally designed driveway would enhance the visual appeal of the property and the surrounding street, contributing positively to the neighbourhood’s character.

Electric charging point: It will allow an electric charging point to be installed at the property so a future vehicle can be charged at the home

Sustainable Drainage Solutions: I intend to use permeable materials in constructing the driveway to comply with Sustainable Urban Drainage Systems (SuDS) guidance, reducing surface water runoff and minimising any impact on local drainage infrastructure.

I am aware of the bus shelter but I believe there is sufficient space to create the crossover, and space on the driveway to turn the vehicle around to drive off with the vehicle front facing. There are many properties that have a crossover on this road and many properties in the area that have one with a bus shelter in close proximity. 

There could also be a discussion to be had with TFL for the relocation of the bus shelter a few doors down outside no 64 and 66. Alternatively, the shelter could be changed to a dolly stop.
